blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume

name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched

concurrency:

      # gh-1503: byte-consistent copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 resolve step

      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough

      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZA…

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import sys
import threading
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

    ErrorPattern,

from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment

# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# The token itself is guarded against digit/dot adjacency —
# `(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])` (gh-1592 review): `\b429\b` still matched the
# `429` inside decimals like `0.429` / `429.5` (`.` is a non-word char,
# so both sides of the token were boundaries), letting echoed output that
# pairs a decimal with rate-limit wording re-trigger the
# misclassification; the lookarounds keep every real shape (`429: …`,
# `HTTP/1.1 429 …`, `"code": 429`) while rejecting `0.429`, `429.5`,
# `1429`.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE
# only; the `^` anchors each attempt to a line start so classification
# stays linear over multi-MB tee'd streams, and the `[^\r\n]*` spans keep

    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*" + _429_TOKEN + r"[^\r\n]*"
)

    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR = "/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs"

_REAP_TIMEOUT_SEC = 60.0
_REAP_ESCALATION_TIMEOUT_SEC = 10.0

# ONE process-level disposition per signal, held on behalf of every live

# (Review round 2, PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sD_xd: a bare

So harbor's installed agents each convert their native logs into ATIF `trajectory.json` written to `self.logs_dir` (i.e. `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` on the host after sync). The FaAgent adapter does NOT do this — so after upload, the trial would lack a `trajectory_path`. That confirms Gap 2: we need to add an ATIF export.

Two options:
a) Convert fa session JSONL → ATIF in Python inside fa_agent.py (adapter-side), similar to other agents like copilot_cli which does `_convert_jsonl_to_trajectory`.
b) Add ATIF export to Dart lib/src/trajectory/ and have the fa CLI emit it.

The ticket says: "we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (lib/src/trajectory/ already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home)."

Since harbor does NOT convert for installed agents (each agent implements its own conversion), we need to add an ATIF export. The natural home per the ticket: `lib/src/trajectory/` — a Dart-side ATIF exporter from the TrajectorySnapshot. But the adapter needs the trajectory.json in the agent logs dir. The fa CLI runs inside the container; the session JSONL is at /logs/agent/fah-sessions. The adapter could run a headless `fa trajectory` export... Actually simpler: the Dart CLI could emit an ATIF trajectory.json next to the session (or the adapter converts). 

Let me look at the ATIF model (harbor.models.trajectories) to know the schema, then look at trajectory_export.dart to see existing exporters.

Also there's an existing `fa trajectory` headless subcommand. Maybe the cleanest: add an ATIF export format to `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` (whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home per ticket), exposed via `fa trajectory export --format atif` or via the existing export CLI, then fa_agent.py invokes `fa trajectory export --format atif --output /logs/agent/trajectory.json` after the run inside the container (post-run, before logs sync), or the adapter converts on the host.

Wait — but where does trajectory.json need to be? `self.logs_dir` on host = trial dir's agent logs downloaded from /logs/agent. Harbor syncs /logs/agent → host logs_dir. So writing /logs/agent/trajectory.json inside the container post-run works. But doing the export inside the container requires the session files still present (they are, at /logs/agent/fah-sessions) and `fa` available — it is.

Alternatively adapter-side (host) conversion: the adapter has access to host trial dir logs after sync... but the sync happens in harbor's Trial flow after run() completes; populate_context_post_run is where usage extraction happens on host. Actually copilot_cli converts on the host from synced logs. That's cleaner: implement ATIF conversion in Python in fa_agent.py from the synced fah-sessions JSONL? But ticket says lib/src/trajectory/ is "the natural home".

Hmm. Let me check `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` to see what exists and what CLI surface exists (`fa trajectory` subcommand with export?). Then decide.

Let me also check the test tree for trajectory export tests, and check how `fa trajectory` headless command works (bin/fah.dart routes). The headless subcommand: `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [--json] [--at N]`. No export subcommand headless yet? The header's copy menu uses trajectory_export.dart exporters.

Design plan emerging:
1. Dart: add `atif.dart` in lib/src/trajectory/ — converts a TrajectorySnapshot to an ATIF JSON document (matching harbor's ATIF schema). Export it from the barrel (grouped append-only).
2. Wire a headless export: `fa trajectory export [sessionId] --format atif --output <path>` (or add `--format atif` to existing?). Check bin/fah.dart routing.
3. fa_agent.py: after run completes, exec in container `fa trajectory export ... --output /logs/agent/trajectory.json` (or adapter-side post-sync conversion on host from fah-sessions). If the agent is killed (timeout), run() raises TimeoutError and the export might be skipped — but the trajectory should still be written (erored trials... well for leaderboard only rewarded trials matter). Writing ATIF from the adapter on the host post-sync handles all cases uniformly and doesn't depend on in-container fa. But conversion logic in Python duplicates the Dart logic and drifts.

But if the trial crashes hard / container destroyed, no trajectory. Leaderboard requires zero infra-erored trials anyway.

"""Trajectory model for ATIF (Agent Trajectory Interchange Format)."""

from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator

from harbor.models.trajectories.agent import Agent
from harbor.models.trajectories.final_metrics import FinalMetrics
from harbor.models.trajectories.step import Step


class Trajectory(BaseModel):
    """Agent Trajectory in ATIF (Agent Trajectory Interchange Format)."""

    schema_version: Literal[
        "ATIF-v1.0",
        "ATIF-v1.1",
        "ATIF-v1.2",
        "ATIF-v1.3",
        "ATIF-v1.4",
        "ATIF-v1.5",
        "ATIF-v1.6",
        "ATIF-v1.7",
        "ATIF-v1.8",
    ] = Field(
        default="ATIF-v1.8",
        description="String defining ATIF compatibility",
    )
    session_id: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Identifier for the agent run this trajectory belongs to. Scoped "
            "to the run, NOT to an individual trajectory document: multiple "
            "Trajectory objects MAY share the same `session_id` when they "
            "represent the same logical run (e.g., a parent trajectory and "
            "its embedded subagents, or a trajectory and its continuation "
            "segments linked via `continued_trajectory_ref`). Therefore "
            "`session_id`s within a parent's `subagent_trajectories` array "
            "are NOT required to be unique. Use `trajectory_id` when a "
            "per-trajectory-document unique identifier is required (e.g., "
            "for `SubagentTrajectoryRef` resolution). Optional since "
            "ATIF-v1.7; producers SHOULD set this on root trajectories for "
            "run-level traceability, and MAY omit it on embedded subagents "
            "that inherit the parent's run identity."
        ),
    )
    trajectory_id: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Canonical per-trajectory-document identifier, distinct from "
            "`session_id`. Unlike `session_id` (which is run-scoped and MAY "
            "be shared), `trajectory_id` uniquely identifies THIS trajectory "
            "object. Used to resolve `SubagentTrajectoryRef` entries against "
            "the root's `subagent_trajectories` array without overloading "
            "`session_id`'s run-scoped semantics. Optional on standalone "
            "trajectories, but REQUIRED on any trajectory embedded in a "
            "parent's `subagent_trajectories` array. `trajectory_id`s within "
            "a single parent's `subagent_trajectories` array MUST be unique. "
            "Added in ATIF-v1.7."
        ),
    )
    agent: Agent = Field(
        default=...,
        description="Object specifying the agent configuration",
    )
    steps: list[Step] = Field(
        default=...,
        min_length=1,
        description="Array of step objects representing the complete interaction history",
    )
    notes: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Custom information, design notes, or explanations",
    )
    final_metrics: FinalMetrics | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Summary metrics for the entire trajectory",
    )
    continued_trajectory_ref: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Reference to the continuation trajectory file if this trajectory is continued in another file",
    )
    extra: dict[str, Any] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Custom root-level metadata",
    )
    subagent_trajectories: list["Trajectory"] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Array of embedded subagent trajectories. Each element is a complete, "
            "independently-valid ATIF Trajectory with its own schema_version, "
            "agent, and step_id sequence starting at 1. Enables single-file "
            "storage of multi-agent workflows: when a "
            "SubagentTrajectoryRef.trajectory_path is null, consumers resolve "
            "the reference by matching SubagentTrajectoryRef.trajectory_id "
            "against Trajectory.trajectory_id of entries in this array. "
            "Uniqueness rules: every embedded subagent MUST set `trajectory_id`, "
            "and `trajectory_id`s within this array MUST be unique. "
            "`session_id`, by contrast, is run-scoped and MAY collide across "
            "siblings (or match the parent) when all trajectories belong to "
            "the same logical run; embedded subagents MAY also omit "
            "`session_id` entirely to inherit the parent's run identity. "
            "Added in ATIF-v1.7."
        ),
    )

    model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}

    def to_json_dict(self, exclude_none: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Export trajectory to a dictionary suitable for JSON serialization.

        Args:
            exclude_none: If True, exclude fields with None values from output.

        Returns:
            Dictionary representation of the trajectory.
        """
        return self.model_dump(exclude_none=exclude_none, mode="json")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_step_ids(self) -> "Trajectory":
        """Validate that step_ids are sequential starting from 1."""
        for i, step in enumerate(self.steps):
            expected_step_id = i + 1
            if step.step_id != expected_step_id:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"steps[{i}].step_id: expected {expected_step_id} "
                    f"(sequential from 1), got {step.step_id}"
                )
        return self

        """Every embedded subagent must carry a unique, non-null `trajectory_id`.

        Embedded subagents are resolved by matching
        `SubagentTrajectoryRef.trajectory_id` against

from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator, model_validator

from harbor.models.trajectories.content import ContentPart
from harbor.models.trajectories.metrics import Metrics
from harbor.models.trajectories.observation import Observation
from harbor.models.trajectories.tool_call import ToolCall


class Step(BaseModel):

    step_id: int = Field(
        default=...,
        ge=1,
        description="Ordinal index of the turn (starting from 1)",
    )
    timestamp: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when this step occurred",
    )
    source: Literal["system", "user", "agent"] = Field(
        default=...,
        description="The originator of this step",
    )
    model_name: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The specific LLM model used for this turn. Omission implies the model "
            "defined in the root-level agent config."
        ),
    )
    reasoning_effort: str | float | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Qualitative or quantitative measure of effort",
    )
    message: str | list[ContentPart] = Field(
        default=...,
        description=(
            "The dialogue message. String for text-only content, or array of "
            "ContentPart for multimodal content (added in ATIF-v1.6)."
        ),
    )
    reasoning_content: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="The agent's explicit internal reasoning",
    )
    tool_calls: list[ToolCall] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Array of structured objects for the agent's actions",
    )
    observation: Observation | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Environment feedback/result after actions or system events",
    )
    metrics: Metrics | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="LLM operational and confidence data for this step",
    )
    is_copied_context: bool | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Indicates whether this step was copied from a previous trajectory "
            "for context (e.g., during continuation after summarization). "
            "Steps marked as copied context should not be included in training data "
            "as they represent previously-trained interactions. "
            "Added in ATIF-v1.5."
        ),
    )
    llm_call_count: int | None = Field(
        default=None,
        ge=0,
        description=(
            "Number of LLM inferences this step represents. When >1, metrics are "
            "aggregated across multiple LLM calls. When 1, the step represents exactly "
            "one inference. When 0 on a `source: 'agent'` step, the step represents a "
            "deterministic (non-LLM) dispatch; `metrics` and `reasoning_content` MUST "
            "be absent in that case. When null, the producer did not track this "
            "(backward-compatible default). Added in ATIF-v1.7."
        ),
    )
    extra: dict[str, Any] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Custom step-level metadata",
    )

    model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}

    @field_validator("timestamp")
    @classmethod
    def validate_timestamp(cls, v: str | None) -> str | None:
        if v is not None:
            try:
                datetime.fromisoformat(v.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
            except ValueError as e:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid ISO 8601 timestamp: {e}")
        return v

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_agent_only_fields(self) -> "Step":
        if self.source != "agent":
            agent_only_fields = [
                "model_name",
                "reasoning_effort",
                "reasoning_content",
                "tool_calls",
                "metrics",
            ]
            for field in agent_only_fields:
                if getattr(self, field) is not None:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Field '{field}' is only applicable when source is 'agent', "
                        f"but source is '{self.source}'"
                    )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_llm_call_count_zero_fields(self) -> "Step":

        When ``llm_call_count == 0`` on a ``source: "agent"`` step, the step
        represents a deterministic (non-LLM) dispatch. LLM-specific fields
        (``metrics``, ``reasoning_content``) MUST be absent on such steps.
        if self.llm_call_count == 0 and self.source == "agent":
            llm_only_fields = ["metrics", "reasoning_content"]
            for field in llm_only_fields:
                if getattr(self, field) is not None:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Field '{field}' must be absent when llm_call_count is 0 "
                        f"(deterministic dispatch on a 'source: agent' step)"
                    )
        return self

from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator, model_validator

# Canonical audio MIME types, chosen to cover what multimodal and transcription
# APIs actually accept: Gemini audio understanding (wav, mp3, aiff, aac, ogg,
# flac), OpenAI transcription (flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, webm),
# and `audio/webm`, which is what a browser's MediaRecorder produces and so what
# human-recorded task data usually arrives as.
AudioMediaType = Literal[
    "audio/wav",
    "audio/mpeg",
    "audio/mp4",
    "audio/aac",
    "audio/ogg",
    "audio/flac",
    "audio/webm",
    "audio/aiff",
]

# Aliases producers emit in place of the registered MIME type, normalized on the
# way in so consumers only ever see one spelling per format. `audio/mp3` is the
# important one: it is not a registered type, but the Gemini API documents and
# emits it, so a producer copying a provider response verbatim would otherwise
# fail validation.
_AUDIO_MEDIA_TYPE_ALIASES = {
    "audio/mp3": "audio/mpeg",
    "audio/mpga": "audio/mpeg",
    "audio/x-mpeg": "audio/mpeg",
    "audio/x-wav": "audio/wav",
    "audio/wave": "audio/wav",
    "audio/vnd.wave": "audio/wav",
    "audio/x-m4a": "audio/mp4",
    "audio/m4a": "audio/mp4",
    "audio/x-aac": "audio/aac",
    "audio/x-flac": "audio/flac",
    "audio/x-aiff": "audio/aiff",
}


class ImageSource(BaseModel):

    media_type: Literal["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/gif", "image/webp"] = Field(

        default=...,

blocks.text:
Confirmed: harbor expects `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` (ATIF), uploaded via packager as `paths.trajectory_path`. The FaAgent doesn't produce it — Gap 2 confirmed.

Design decision: Where to implement the ATIF export?

Option A (Dart): `lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart` with `exportAtifJson(TrajectorySnapshot snapshot, {agentName, agentVersion, modelName})` producing an ATIF-v1.8 document. Then wire a headless `fa trajectory export` verb that resolves the session, builds the snapshot, and writes the ATIF JSON to a file (or stdout). The adapter (fa_agent.py) then runs post-trial in the container: `fa trajectory export --format atif --output /logs/agent/trajectory.json`... but wait, subagent sessions and the main session: the ATIF root trajectory should be the main session; subagents could be embedded. Keep scope reasonable: main session trajectory + optional subagent_trajectories from child session files? The snapshot only covers one session. Simplest: export the resolved session's snapshot. Subagent embedding would need reading child sessions — too much for this card; the leaderboard static analysis just needs `trajectory_path` present and ATIF-valid. I'll note subagents as future work, or... Actually `fa` bench runs may use subagents. But keep the scope: main-session ATIF. Hmm, but reward-hacking audit (/judge) reads trajectories — main session trajectory contains tool calls and observations, good enough.

Option B (Python adapter-side): convert fah-sessions JSONL → ATIF in fa_agent.py. Duplicates schema knowledge in Python; but no Dart CLI plumbing needed, and can run host-side after logs sync (populate_context_post_run). Actually host-side has a wrinkle: populate_context_post_run writes to host logs_dir — that's exactly where other agents write trajectory.json (e.g., copilot_cli writes `self.logs_dir / "trajectory.json"` post-run on the host). That pattern exists and is proven.

The ticket explicitly points at lib/src/trajectory/ as "the natural home". I'll do Option A: Dart ATIF exporter + headless export verb + adapter invoking it in-container post-run (best-effort, after fa exits, before/after audit). In-container export works even on killed trials since it's a separate exec. But careful: if the trial container is torn down... the export exec happens in run() before returning, so fine.

Actually wait — which session does the export verb resolve? The adapter runs `fa --session-root /logs/agent/fah-sessions -p ...`. The main session is the most recent in that root. `resolveTrajectorySession(repo, null)` resolves most recent. Good — `fa trajectory export` with no id resolves most recent.

But there's a subtlety: `fa trajectory export` must run with `--session-root`. CliArgs has `sessionRoot`. Good.

Also need agent name/version/model in the ATIF doc: FaAgent version is `_VERSION = "0.1.0"`; the agent name "fa". Model name — from the provider config (FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG JSON, model field). The adapter knows the model. So adapter could pass `--agent-name fa --agent-version <ver> --model <model>`? Hmm, but maybe cleaner: `fa --version` output? Keep it explicit flags on the export verb: `--agent-name`, `--agent-version`, `--model`, `--output`. The adapter passes model from FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG and version from `fa --version` output... simpler: adapter hardcodes/derives. Actually the CLI knows its own version. Let the Dart export verb default agent name to "fa" and version to the CLI's package version (there's likely a version constant — check `fa --version` implementation). Model: the session JSONL may contain provider/model info? The assistant records carry `provider` and `model` fields (TrajectoryAssistantRecord has provider/model). So the exporter can derive model_name from the first assistant record with a model. Good — self-contained.

Now, check how `fa --version` works to get the version constant.

Also need to check: does the ATIF validator exist in harbor (`trajectory_validator.py`) — I can validate my generated ATIF in tests using the harbor package? The bench tests install harbor in CI; but for Dart unit tests, I'll write a Dart test that checks schema-shape basics. Could also add a Python test in bench/harbor_fa that validates generated fixture ATIF against harbor's validator if harbor is installed (skip if not). Let me check how existing python tests handle harbor import — test_fa_agent.py imports harbor? Let me check.

Let me now check:
1. cli_args.dart trajectory parsing full block.
2. bin/fah.dart routing of trajectory command + version constant.
3. How TrajectorySnapshotBuilder projects records (trajectorySnapshotOf in trajectory_commands?).
4. trajectory_tui.dart / trajectory_commands.dart exports (trajectorySnapshotOf, resolveTrajectorySession, trajectoryVerbRecords).
5. barrel export list for trajectory subsystem.

# gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

### References

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).
- Community submissions closed at the time of writing for 2.1 and 4.0 — this card is readiness, not an immediate submission.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash

from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment

_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:

import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output

# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every

    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

_POLL_SEC = 5.0

# The pkill pattern: the `[f]a` bracket trick (gh-1556 AC1) — a plain

So harbor's installed agents each convert their native logs into ATIF `trajectory.json` written to `self.logs_dir` (i.e. `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` on the host after sync). The FaAgent adapter does NOT do this — so after upload, the trial would lack a `trajectory_path`. That confirms Gap 2: we need to add an ATIF export.

Two options:
a) Convert fa session JSONL → ATIF in Python inside fa_agent.py (adapter-side), similar to other agents like copilot_cli which does `_convert_jsonl_to_trajectory`.
b) Add ATIF export to Dart lib/src/trajectory/ and have the fa CLI emit it.

The ticket says: "we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (lib/src/trajectory/ already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home)."

Since harbor does NOT convert for installed agents (each agent implements its own conversion), we need to add an ATIF export. The natural home per the ticket: `lib/src/trajectory/` — a Dart-side ATIF exporter from the TrajectorySnapshot. But the adapter needs the trajectory.json in the agent logs dir. The fa CLI runs inside the container; the session JSONL is at /logs/agent/fah-sessions. The adapter could run a headless `fa trajectory` export... Actually simpler: the Dart CLI could emit an ATIF trajectory.json next to the session (or the adapter converts). 

Let me look at the ATIF model (harbor.models.trajectories) to know the schema, then look at trajectory_export.dart to see existing exporters.

Also there's an existing `fa trajectory` headless subcommand. Maybe the cleanest: add an ATIF export format to `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` (whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home per ticket), exposed via `fa trajectory export --format atif` or via the existing export CLI, then fa_agent.py invokes `fa trajectory export --format atif --output /logs/agent/trajectory.json` after the run inside the container (post-run, before logs sync), or the adapter converts on the host.

Wait — but where does trajectory.json need to be? `self.logs_dir` on host = trial dir's agent logs downloaded from /logs/agent. Harbor syncs /logs/agent → host logs_dir. So writing /logs/agent/trajectory.json inside the container post-run works. But doing the export inside the container requires the session files still present (they are, at /logs/agent/fah-sessions) and `fa` available — it is.

Alternatively adapter-side (host) conversion: the adapter has access to host trial dir logs after sync... but the sync happens in harbor's Trial flow after run() completes; populate_context_post_run is where usage extraction happens on host. Actually copilot_cli converts on the host from synced logs. That's cleaner: implement ATIF conversion in Python in fa_agent.py from the synced fah-sessions JSONL? But ticket says lib/src/trajectory/ is "the natural home".

Hmm. Let me check `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart` to see what exists and what CLI surface exists (`fa trajectory` subcommand with export?). Then decide.

Let me also check the test tree for trajectory export tests, and check how `fa trajectory` headless command works (bin/fah.dart routes). The headless subcommand: `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [--json] [--at N]`. No export subcommand headless yet? The header's copy menu uses trajectory_export.dart exporters.

Design plan emerging:
1. Dart: add `atif.dart` in lib/src/trajectory/ — converts a TrajectorySnapshot to an ATIF JSON document (matching harbor's ATIF schema). Export it from the barrel (grouped append-only).
2. Wire a headless export: `fa trajectory export [sessionId] --format atif --output <path>` (or add `--format atif` to existing?). Check bin/fah.dart routing.
3. fa_agent.py: after run completes, exec in container `fa trajectory export ... --output /logs/agent/trajectory.json` (or adapter-side post-sync conversion on host from fah-sessions). Which is better for robustness? If the agent is killed (timeout), run() raises TimeoutError and the export might be skipped — but the trajectory should still be written (erored trials... well for leaderboard only rewarded trials matter). Writing ATIF from the adapter on the host post-sync handles all cases uniformly and doesn't depend on in-container fa. But conversion logic in Python duplicates the Dart logic and drifts.

Actually — writing it in Dart and invoking in-container has a wrinkle: the kill paths (SIGTERM kill of fa) terminate the process; a post-run export exec would be a separate exec so it still works after fa exits. But if the trial crashes hard / container destroyed, no trajectory. Leaderboard requires zero infra-erored trials anyway.

Alternatively adapter-side: after logs sync, host-side Python converts session JSONL → ATIF. Session JSONL format is the harness's own; the Dart side already knows how to project it. Duplicating in Python is drift-prone. But the ATIF schema is harbor's; Dart code producing ATIF is also fine.

Let me look at what the ticket prefers: "add an ATIF export path (lib/src/trajectory/ already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home)". So Dart-side exporter in lib/src/trajectory/. Then the adapter invokes the headless CLI inside the container post-run (`fa trajectory export --format atif -o /logs/agent/trajectory.json`). The CLI reads its own session JSONL → ATIF. That's the clean path and testable in Dart.

"""Trajectory model for ATIF (Agent Trajectory Interchange Format)."""

from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator

from harbor.models.trajectories.agent import Agent
from harbor.models.trajectories.final_metrics import FinalMetrics
from harbor.models.trajectories.step import Step


class Trajectory(BaseModel):
    """Agent Trajectory in ATIF (Agent Trajectory Interchange Format)."""

    schema_version: Literal[
        "ATIF-v1.0",
        "ATIF-v1.1",
        "ATIF-v1.2",
        "ATIF-v1.3",
        "ATIF-v1.4",
        "ATIF-v1.5",
        "ATIF-v1.6",
        "ATIF-v1.7",
        "ATIF-v1.8",
    ] = Field(
        default="ATIF-v1.8",
        description="String defining ATIF compatibility",
    )
    session_id: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Identifier for the agent run this trajectory belongs to. Scoped "
            "to the run, NOT to an individual trajectory document: multiple "
            "Trajectory objects MAY share the same `session_id` when they "
            "represent the same logical run (e.g., a parent trajectory and "
            "its embedded subagents, or a trajectory and its continuation "
            "segments linked via `continued_trajectory_ref`). Therefore "
            "`session_id`s within a parent's `subagent_trajectories` array "
            "are NOT required to be unique. Use `trajectory_id` when a "
            "per-trajectory-document unique identifier is required (e.g., "
            "for `SubagentTrajectoryRef` resolution). Optional since "
            "ATIF-v1.7; producers SHOULD set this on root trajectories for "
            "run-level traceability, and MAY omit it on embedded subagents "
            "that inherit the parent's run identity."
        ),
    )
    trajectory_id: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Canonical per-trajectory-document identifier, distinct from "
            "`session_id`. Unlike `session_id` (which is run-scoped and MAY "
            "be shared), `trajectory_id` uniquely identifies THIS trajectory "
            "object. Used to resolve `SubagentTrajectoryRef` entries against "
            "the root's `subagent_trajectories` array without overloading "
            "`session_id`'s run-scoped semantics. Optional on standalone "
            "trajectories, but REQUIRED on any trajectory embedded in a "
            "parent's `subagent_trajectories` array. `trajectory_id`s within "
            "a single parent's `subagent_trajectories` array MUST be unique. "
            "Added in ATIF-v1.7."
        ),
    )
    agent: Agent = Field(
        default=...,
        description="Object specifying the agent configuration",
    )
    steps: list[Step] = Field(
        default=...,
        min_length=1,
        description="Array of step objects representing the complete interaction history",
    )
    notes: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Custom information, design notes, or explanations",
    )
    final_metrics: FinalMetrics | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Summary metrics for the entire trajectory",
    )
    continued_trajectory_ref: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Reference to the continuation trajectory file if this trajectory is continued in another file",
    )
    extra: dict[str, Any] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Custom root-level metadata",
    )
    subagent_trajectories: list["Trajectory"] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Array of embedded subagent trajectories. Each element is a complete, "
            "independently-valid ATIF Trajectory with its own schema_version, "
            "agent, and step_id sequence starting at 1. Enables single-file "
            "storage of multi-agent workflows: when a "
            "SubagentTrajectoryRef.trajectory_path is null, consumers resolve "
            "the reference by matching SubagentTrajectoryRef.trajectory_id "
            "against Trajectory.trajectory_id of entries in this array. "
            "Uniqueness rules: every embedded subagent MUST set `trajectory_id`, "
            "and `trajectory_id`s within this array MUST be unique. "
            "`session_id`, by contrast, is run-scoped and MAY collide across "
            "siblings (or match the parent) when all trajectories belong to "
            "the same logical run; embedded subagents MAY also omit "
            "`session_id` entirely to inherit the parent's run identity. "
            "Added in ATIF-v1.7."
        ),
    )

    model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}

    def to_json_dict(self, exclude_none: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Export trajectory to a dictionary suitable for JSON serialization.

        Args:
            exclude_none: If True, exclude fields with None values from output.

        Returns:
            Dictionary representation of the trajectory.
        """
        return self.model_dump(exclude_none=exclude_none, mode="json")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_step_ids(self) -> "Trajectory":
        """Validate that step_ids are sequential starting from 1."""
        for i, step in enumerate(self.steps):
            expected_step_id = i + 1
            if step.step_id != expected_step_id:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"steps[{i}].step_id: expected {expected_step_id} "
                    f"(sequential from 1), got {step.step_id}"
                )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_embedded_subagent_trajectory_ids(self) -> "Trajectory":
        """Every embedded subagent must carry a unique, non-null `trajectory_id`.

        Embedded subagents are resolved by matching
        `SubagentTrajectoryRef.trajectory_id` against
        `Trajectory.trajectory_id`, so the identifier must be present and
        unique within a parent's `subagent_trajectories` array. Note that
        no such constraint is placed on `session_id` — siblings MAY share
        a `session_id` (or omit it entirely to inherit the parent's) when
        they represent the same logical agent run.
        """

class Step(BaseModel):

    step_id: int = Field(
        default=...,

    timestamp: str | None = Field(
        default=None,

        default=...,

        ),
    )
    reasoning_effort: str | float | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Qualitative or quantitative measure of effort",
    )
    message: str | list[ContentPart] = Field(

        description="Array of structured objects for the agent's actions",
    )
    observation: Observation | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Environment feedback/result after actions or system events",
    )
    metrics: Metrics | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="LLM operational and confidence data for this step",
    )
    is_copied_context: bool | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Indicates whether this step was copied from a previous trajectory "
            "for context (e.g., during continuation after summarization). "
            "Steps marked as copied context should not be included in training data "
            "as they represent previously-trained interactions. "
            "Added in ATIF-v1.5."
        ),
    )
    llm_call_count: int | None = Field(
        default=None,
        ge=0,
        description=(
            "Number of LLM inferences this step represents. When >1, metrics are "
            "aggregated across multiple LLM calls. When 1, the step represents exactly "
            "one inference. When 0 on a `source: 'agent'` step, the step represents a "
            "deterministic (non-LLM) dispatch; `metrics` and `reasoning_content` MUST "
            "be absent in that case. When null, the producer did not track this "
            "(backward-compatible default). Added in ATIF-v1.7."
        ),
    )
    extra: dict[str, Any] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Custom step-level metadata",
    )

    model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}

    @field_validator("timestamp")
    @classmethod
    def validate_timestamp(cls, v: str | None) -> str | None:
        if v is not None:
            try:
                datetime.fromisoformat(v.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
            except ValueError as e:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid ISO 8601 timestamp: {e}")
        return v

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_agent_only_fields(self) -> "Step":
        if self.source != "agent":
            agent_only_fields = [
                "model_name",
                "reasoning_effort",
                "reasoning_content",
                "tool_calls",
                "metrics",
            ]
            for field in agent_only_fields:
                if getattr(self, field) is not None:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Field '{field}' is only applicable when source is 'agent', "
                        f"but source is '{self.source}'"
                    )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_llm_call_count_zero_fields(self) -> "Step":

        When ``llm_call_count == 0`` on a ``source: "agent"`` step, the step
        represents a deterministic (non-LLM) dispatch. LLM-specific fields
        (``metrics``, ``reasoning_content``) MUST be absent on such steps.
        if self.llm_call_count == 0 and self.source == "agent":
            llm_only_fields = ["metrics", "reasoning_content"]
            for field in llm_only_fields:
                if getattr(self, field) is not None:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Field '{field}' must be absent when llm_call_count is 0 "
                        f"(deterministic dispatch on a 'source: agent' step)"
                    )
        return self

# Canonical audio MIME types, chosen to cover what multimodal and transcription
# APIs actually accept: Gemini audio understanding (wav, mp3, aiff, aac, ogg,
# flac), OpenAI transcription (flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, webm),
# and `audio/webm`, which is what a browser's MediaRecorder produces and so what
# human-recorded task data usually arrives as.
AudioMediaType = Literal[
    "audio/wav",
    "audio/mpeg",
    "audio/mp4",
    "audio/aac",
    "audio/ogg",
    "audio/flac",
    "audio/webm",
    "audio/aiff",
]

# Aliases producers emit in place of the registered MIME type, normalized on the
# way in so consumers only ever see one spelling per format. `audio/mp3` is the
# important one: it is not a registered type, but the Gemini API documents and
# emits it, so a producer copying a provider response verbatim would otherwise
# fail validation.
_AUDIO_MEDIA_TYPE_ALIASES = {
    "audio/mp3": "audio/mpeg",
    "audio/mpga": "audio/mpeg",
    "audio/x-mpeg": "audio/mpeg",
    "audio/x-wav": "audio/wav",
    "audio/wave": "audio/wav",
    "audio/vnd.wave": "audio/wav",
    "audio/x-m4a": "audio/mp4",
    "audio/m4a": "audio/mp4",
    "audio/x-aac": "audio/aac",
    "audio/x-flac": "audio/flac",
    "audio/x-aiff": "audio/aiff",
}

Keep scope reasonable: main session trajectory + optional subagent_trajectories from child session files? The snapshot only covers one session. Simplest: export the resolved session's snapshot. Subagent embedding would need reading child sessions — too much for this card; the leaderboard static analysis just needs `trajectory_path` present and ATIF-valid. # gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

### References

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).
- Community submissions closed at the time of writing for 2.1 and 4.0 — this card is readiness, not an immediate submission.
